notes: The effort-based-pricing case study: variable per-checkpoint pricing where failed/looping agent runs still bill — the dataset's clearest failed-actions-consume-credits example.

change_events.description: 'Effort-Based Pricing' replaced flat $0.25/checkpoint — simple tasks under $0.25, complex tasks bundled into one variable-priced checkpoint. Applied to existing subscribers July 1, 2025.
change_events.user_reaction: Initial acceptance; complaints grew with Agent 3

change_events.description: Agent 3 launch triggered cost-unpredictability backlash: users reported ~$1,000/week vs prior $180–200/month, single prompts costing $20, no pre-run estimate, and billing for failed/looping runs. Replit's FAQ disclaims the agent is 'probabilistic... may occasionally make mistakes.'
change_events.notice_period: n/a — product launch with existing meter

snapshots.trial: free Starter tier, limited daily Agent credits

plans.name: Starter
plans.whats_gated: Limited daily Agent credits, 1 published project

limits.throttle_behavior: overage billed to card; user-set budget limits can suspend apps

plans.whats_gated: Replaced retired Teams ($40/user reported): pooled credits, 15 collaborators, 10 parallel agents, most powerful models, 28-day DB rollbacks

limits.throttle_behavior: overage billed in arrears; invoice thresholds $50–$250

usage_meters.rate: variable by computational effort; formerly flat $0.25/checkpoint
usage_meters.overage_behavior: billed to card past credit allotment; budget limits can suspend apps

credits_system.credit_definition: Dollar-denominated credits covering Agent, deployments, database, transfer
credits_system.credit_to_compute_mapping: Opaque per task — effort-based checkpoint price not estimable before a run (core user complaint)
credits_system.expiry: Core: monthly reset, no rollover; Pro: 1-month rollover

predictability.refund_on_failure_policy: none — failed/looping runs bill (FAQ disclaims probabilistic mistakes)
